reason: This passage from Exodus 12:31-51 describes the Passover and the Israelites' departure from Egypt. The text contains no instance of the regular people complaining to their leaders (Moses and Aaron). Rather, it emphasizes obedience: 'וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֖וּ כָּל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ה צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽת־ אַהֲרֹ֖ן' ('All the children of Israel did just as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron'). The passage focuses on compliance with divine instructions, the Passover regulations, and the mechanics of the exodus itself. Since there is no complaint narrative or rebuke against complaining, the stated moral does not apply to this text.
